name: Roche / SWAP (Some Work, All Play)

citations.title: The Happy Runner: Love the Process, Get Faster, Run Longer

description: Joy-emphasizing trail/ultra system from the Roche husband-wife coaching team. Built around aerobic threshold (AeT) work, 30-30 second strides as the signature workout, and 'fast aerobic + short fast' combinations. Anchored to AeT (aerobic threshold) heart rate. Plans cover 50K through 100-mile races, with strong applicability to road marathon as well.
signature: 30-30 strides (30 sec on / 30 sec off) and aerobic threshold-anchored zones, with explicit emphasis on running joyfully
philosophyNarrative: The Roches' SWAP system rests on a counterintuitive observation: many ultrarunners over-train and arrive at races depleted, having sacrificed joy for volume. Their answer is 'Some Work, All Play' — keep the playful spirit central, do the work that matters most, and skip the rest. Five principles: (1) aerobic threshold (AeT) is the master metric — most volume sits below it; (2) the 30-30 stride (30 seconds at fast effort, 30 seconds easy) is the signature workout, used 1-2× weekly to build neuromuscular sharpness without true hard sessions; (3) workouts combine 'fast aerobic' + 'short fast' (e.g., 50 min AeT followed by 6× 30-sec strides) to develop both aerobic and neuromuscular systems efficiently; (4) hill strides on rolling terrain are foundational from week one; (5) wave loading — varying weekly volume and intensity rather than steady linear progression — maintains freshness. The system is more flexible and adaptive than CTS Ultra, with a wider applicability across distances and especially welcoming to runners coming back from injury or burnout.

paceZones.purpose: Active recovery — well below AeT. Used between hard days.
Bulk of weekly running — well below aerobic threshold. Conversational.
Master metric for SWAP. Sustainable for hours. Used in fast aerobic runs and embedded in long runs late in training.
Lactate threshold work. Used sparingly in SWAP — typically only 1× per week and only in the build/peak phases.
Short fast efforts — 30 seconds at near-mile race effort, used in 30-30 sets and hill strides. Builds neuromuscular sharpness.

rpeRange.description: Fast — but the 30-sec duration keeps it sustainable

workouts.name: Aerobic Run
workouts.shortDescription: Easy aerobic run below AeT — bulk of weekly volume

mainSet.cue: Hold HR below AeT. On hills, slow down — pace varies, AeT discipline does not.

workouts.purpose: Aerobic base building. The Roches emphasize quality of easy days — you should finish feeling good, not depleted.
cues: If HR drifts above AeT, slow down or hike
Should feel restorative, not draining
Joy matters — if running feels like a chore today, run shorter

workouts.name: Aerobic + 30-30 Strides
workouts.shortDescription: Aerobic run with 30-30 strides at the end — SWAP's signature combo

mainSet.cue: Fast but controlled — near-mile race effort. The 30-sec duration is long enough to matter, short enough to stay smooth.

workouts.purpose: SWAP's signature combination workout. Builds aerobic capacity (the long aerobic block) AND neuromuscular sharpness (the 30-30s) in one session, without true hard work.
cues: 30-30s should feel quick but never grinding
If 30-30s feel labored, do fewer reps or stop early
Recovery jogs keep moving — don't walk the recoveries

workouts.name: Long Run
workouts.shortDescription: Long aerobic run, with optional AeT segment late in training

mainSet.cue: Hold HR below AeT — even as fatigue accumulates and HR wants to drift up.

workouts.purpose: Endurance building. SWAP long runs vary by race distance — capped at 22 mi for marathon, can extend to 5+ hours for 100-milers.
cues: Time on feet matters more than mileage
Practice race-day fueling on runs over 90 min
On trails, target similar elevation gain to your race

workouts.name: Long Run with AeT Segment
workouts.shortDescription: Long run with 20-40 min at AeT in the middle

mainSet.cue: Lock into AeT effort. Pace varies with terrain — HR is the constant.

workouts.purpose: Builds the ability to hold AeT under accumulated fatigue — the central physiological demand of ultra and marathon racing.
cues: AeT segment is sustainable — should not feel like racing
Practice race fueling and gear during the run
If AeT pace drops significantly during segment, end early — you're fatigued

workouts.name: Hill Strides
workouts.shortDescription: 8-10× ~10-second strides up moderate hills, full recovery

warmup.description: Easy run to base of hill

mainSet.cue: Fast and explosive uphill — 10 seconds of work, full recovery walk down.

workouts.purpose: Strength + neuromuscular work. Hill grade does the work — you don't need pure flat speed. Used 1× weekly in foundation and build phases.
cues: Pick a hill ~5-8% grade
Walk down for full recovery
Build to top speed gradually within the 10 seconds

workouts.name: AnT Workout
workouts.shortDescription: Lactate threshold intervals — used sparingly in build/peak

mainSet.cue: AnT effort — about 1-hour race pace. Even effort across all reps.

workouts.purpose: Lactate threshold development. SWAP uses AnT work sparingly — once per week max, only in build and peak phases.
cues: Even effort — first rep at the same intensity as the last
If reps slow significantly, end the workout
AnT is harder than AeT — respect the recovery requirement

workouts.name: Recovery Run
workouts.shortDescription: Very easy short run between hard efforts

mainSet.description: Very easy run well below AeT
mainSet.cue: Restorative effort — should leave you feeling better.

workouts.purpose: Active recovery. SWAP encourages skipping recovery runs entirely if fatigued — joy and freshness matter.
cues: If you don't feel better at the end, you ran too hard
Skipping is allowed — SWAP values freshness
Walking is fine

phases.name: Foundation
phases.focus: Aerobic base + 30-30 strides + hill strides. No AnT work yet.
phases.athleteNarrative: Welcome to the SWAP foundation phase. This is where you build the aerobic engine and learn the rhythm of 30-30 strides. Two short fast sessions per week (30-30s and hill strides) keep you sharp without true hard work. Most weekly running is below aerobic threshold — finish runs feeling good, not depleted. Joy comes first; everything follows from that.

phases.name: Build
phases.focus: Add AeT segments to long runs. Begin AnT (threshold) workouts once per week. Continue 30-30s and hill strides.
phases.athleteNarrative: Build phase. AeT segments enter long runs — 20-30 min at aerobic threshold builds the ability to sustain race pace under fatigue. Once a week, an AnT (lactate threshold) workout is added. The 30-30s and hill strides continue throughout — they're the rhythm of SWAP.

phases.name: Peak
phases.focus: Peak AeT volume in long runs. Race-specific terrain practice. Peak weekly volume.
phases.athleteNarrative: Peak phase. The longest AeT segments occur here. For mountain ultras, target similar vertical to your race. AnT workouts continue once per week. Wave loading is crucial — you'll have heavy weeks and lighter weeks rather than steady linear progression.

phases.name: Taper
phases.focus: Reduce volume; preserve 30-30s and hill strides for sharpness; arrive joyful.
phases.athleteNarrative: Taper. Volume drops, but 30-30s and hill strides continue at reduced volume so you stay sharp. The Roches emphasize: arrive at the start line feeling FRESH and EXCITED, not exhausted. Skip workouts if you don't feel up for them. Sleep, eat, hydrate, smile.

weeklyPatterns.notes: Foundation 5-day. Tuesday 30-30s + Thursday hill strides + Sunday long run. No AnT work yet.
Build 5-day. AnT Tuesday + 30-30s Thursday + hill strides Saturday + Long run Sunday with optional AeT segment.
Build 6-day. Adds Monday recovery run for higher weekly volume.
Peak 5-day. Hill strides drop to make room for peak Long run AeT segments.
Recovery week — every 3-4 weeks. Drops AnT, keeps 30-30s, cuts long run.

taper.notes: SWAP taper is short and joyful — 2 weeks at 70%/45%. 30-30s and hill strides preserved at low volume to keep neuromuscular sharpness without depletion.

strengthRecommendation.philosophy: Strong recommendation: 2× weekly strength sessions of 20-40 min. Focus on glute/hip strength, single-leg work, core stability. The Roches see strength as foundational for both performance and durability.

crossTrainingRecommendation.intensityGuidance: Cross-training, especially yoga and hiking, are explicitly encouraged. Yoga supports joy and recovery; hiking adds vertical gain without running impact. Easy effort only.

restrictions.rule: Requires AeT (aerobic threshold) measurement for accurate zone targeting. Without HR data and a known AeT, the system relies on RPE — workable but less precise.
restrictions.warningMessage: SWAP works best with a known AeT (aerobic threshold). Without HR data, you'll need to self-regulate by RPE — possible, but the AeT-anchored precision is part of what makes the system effective.

restrictions.rule: Beginners can use SWAP but benefit from a longer foundation phase. The 30-30 strides and AnT work assume baseline running fitness.
restrictions.warningMessage: SWAP is accessible but assumes some running history. For first-time runners or returning from extended layoff, Higdon Novice is gentler.

invariants: 30-30 strides included weekly throughout the program (except race week which has reduced volume)
Hill strides included weekly in foundation and build phases
AnT work introduced only in build phase, max 1× per week
Long run cap at 35% of weekly mileage
Wave loading: vary weekly volume by ±10-15% rather than steady linear progression
Skip workouts when fatigued — SWAP values freshness over rigid adherence
30-30s never go to maximum effort — fast but smooth
